extracted.intended_audience: vessel owners and agents; shipbuilders; airport/operators; regulated parties and interested members of the public who submit comments or applications to Federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for applications, certifications, and public comments in response to Federal Register proposed rulemakings and agency notices (including technical application itemization for vessel measurement, deadlines and formats for public comments, airspace designation descriptions, and internal delegation thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for measurement under optional dual tonnage method — required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the owner or his agent for measurement of a vessel under the provisions of the optional dual tonnage method shall be submitted in duplicate together with supporting plans or sketches to the customs officer in charge of the district in which the vessel is or will be located. The application shall include the following information (See figures 55, 56, and 57): (1) Molded depth at midship section from second deck at side. (2) Depth used with tonnage mark table. (3) Length of shorter portion of stepped second deck if any. (4) Total length of longer and shorter portions of stepped second deck. (5) Length used with tonnage mark table. (6) Height of step (break) in the second deck, if any. (7) Distance from the molded line of the second deck or equivalent to the upper edge of the tonnage mark. (8) Molded draft to the upper edge of the tonnage mark. (9) Freeboard from the loadline certificate. (10) Molded draft to the loadline. (11) Distance from the centerline of the loadline disk to the apex of the triangle on the tonnage mark. (12) Distance from the deck line to the tonnage mark. (13) Distance from the molded line of the second deck or equivalent to the deck line for freeboard. (14) Allowance for fresh water and tropical waters (%8 of the molded draft to the upper edge of the tonnage mark). (15) The name and official number of the vessel, if assigned. (16) Builder’s name and hull number if official number has not been assigned. (17) Time and place vessel will be available for measurement. (18) Whether two sets of tonnages are desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the application in duplicate with supporting plans/sketches to the district customs officer where the vessel is/will be located. The listed items are mandatory elements of the application; see referenced figures for measurement conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner may request confirmation of proposed tonnage-mark location
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may request confirmation of the proposed location of the tonnage mark based on the information contained in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an owner wants assurance of where the tonnage mark will be placed, they should request confirmation when filing the application; the request triggers review based on the submitted measurements and plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency advisement on application copy regarding measurement method and correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: On a copy of the application or on an attachment thereto, the owner shall be advised: (1) That the vessel will be measured under the provisions of the optional dual-tonnage method; and (2) Whether the proposed location of the tonnage mark determined according to the information furnished on the application is correct under the provisions of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The customs officer will annotate the application copy (or attach a note) to inform the owner both of the measurement method to be used and of whether the proposed mark location complies with regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement for placement of tonnage mark before certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a certificate of admeasurement shall be issued for a vessel requiring a tonnage mark, the owner or his agent shall certify that a tonnage mark has been placed on each side of the vessel in accordance with the pertinent provisions of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification by the American Bureau of Shipping or other recognized classification society that the tonnage marks have been applied under the provisions of the regulations shall be accepted as evidence of proper marking. In the absence of such certification, the customs officer in charge may at any time cause a tonnage mark to be verified on a vessel in his district.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment submission period and format (Customs proposal example)
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice is published pursuant to section 4 of the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. 1003). Prior to final action on the proposal consideration will be given to any data, views, or arguments pertaining thereto which are submitted in writing to the Commissioner of Customs, Washington, D.C., and received within a period of 60 days from the date of the publication of this notice in the Federal Register. No hearings will be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be written and received within the stated period (60 days in this instance) to be considered. The notice cites APA authority and explicitly states whether hearings will be held; here, no hearings will be held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of comment period and instructions for filing (U.S. Standards for Grades of Green Olives example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for receiving written data, views, or arguments from interested parties in connection with the proposed revision of the U.S. Standards for Grades of Green Olives has been extended to April 1, 1966. All persons who wish to submit written data, views, or arguments within the additional time should file the same — in duplicate — with the Hearing Clerk, Room 112-A, U.S. Department of Agriculture, Washington, D.C., 20250, on or before April 1, 1966. Comments received will be available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may extend comment deadlines for good cause (here, industry requests and need for further study). When extended, the notice specifies filing format (in duplicate), the receiving office and that submitted comments will be available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA public comment procedures for airspace proposals (submission format, deadlines, and conferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may submit such written data, views or arguments as they may desire. Communications should be submitted in triplicate to the Area Manager, Atlanta Area Office (or to the Chief, Air Traffic Division, Alaskan Region, as specified). All communications received within 30 days (30 days for some proposals; 45 days for certain Alaskan proposals) after publication of this notice in the Federal Register will be considered before action is taken on the proposed amendment. No hearing is contemplated at this time, but arrangements for informal conferences with Federal Aviation Agency officials may be made. Any data, views or arguments presented during such conferences must also be submitted in writing in accordance with this notice in order to become part of the record for consideration. The proposal contained in this notice may be changed in the light of comments received. The official docket will be available for examination by interested persons at the listed regional office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the required number of copies (triplicate), the specific receiving office and attention line, and the deadline (varies by notice). Informal conferences do not substitute for written submission — any material presented must be put in writing to be part of the record. Docket location is provided for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airspace designation criteria (transition areas and control zones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed transition areas are described by explicit geometric and navigational criteria: e.g., 'designated as that airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface within an 8-mile radius of the Johns Island Airport (latitude 32°42'00" N., longitude 80°00'00" W.), excluding the portion within R-6003 and the Charleston, S.C., 700-foot transition area.' Other designations specify radii (5-mile, 8-mile), altitude floors (700 feet, 1,200 feet), radials and distances from VORTAC/TACAN, and specific exclusions or overlaps with existing zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airspace proposals must specify coordinates, radii, altitude floors, radial corridors (e.g., 'within 2 miles each side of the Jacksonville VORTAC 001° radial'), and any exclusions. These geometric definitions are the controlling criterion for the proposed designation; supporting instrument procedures are often cited as the operational need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose statements for airspace actions (need and protective intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed transition area is needed for the protection of IFR operations at the [named] Airport. A prescribed instrument approach procedure utilizing the [named VORTAC/TACAN] is proposed in conjunction with the designation of this transition area. The proposed actions would alter the configuration of the Control Zone extension to provide protective airspace for prescribed instrument procedures and would provide protective airspace for aircraft executing portions of the prescribed instrument approaches, missed approaches, departures, and holding procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airspace amendments must articulate the safety/operational rationale (e.g., protection for IFR procedures) and how the geometric changes provide the required protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The official docket will be available for examination by interested persons at the listed regional or agency office (e.g., Southern Regional Office, Federal Aviation Agency, Room 724, 3400 Whipple Street, East Point, Ga.; Office of the Regional Counsel, Anchorage, Alaska). Comments received will be available for public inspection (e.g., USDA Hearing Clerk example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices specify where and when the administrative record/docket and submitted comments may be inspected; interested parties should consult the named office for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of procurement and contracting authority with dollar thresholds (National Park Service examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Assistant may issue purchase orders not in excess of $2,500 for supplies or equipment. Chief Park Ranger, Chief Park Naturalist, and Maintenance Superintendent may issue purchase orders not in excess of $100. (Jefferson National Expansion Memorial: Assistant Superintendent and Administrative Officer may execute contracts not in excess of $50,000; Procurement and Property Management Officer up to $2,500; Procurement and Property Management Assistant up to $300.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders explicitly set dollar ceilings for delegated contracting authority and state that actions must conform to applicable regulations, statutory authority, and availability of allotted funds/appropriations. They also note revocation/supersession of prior orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation limits for Bureau of Public Roads / Federal Highway Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the authority vested in the Secretary of Commerce and subject to policies/directives, the Federal Highway Administrator is delegated the authority to perform the functions vested in the Secretary of Commerce under Title 23, United States Code, Highways, and under the Act approved July 14, 1960, and the Highway Beautification Act of 1965, except with respect to the apportionment of Federal-aid highway funds among the States and the promulgation of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation statements identify both the scope of authority delegated and explicit exclusions (apportionment of funds and promulgation of regulations). Such delegations are subject to departmental policies and directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: General functions and program responsibilities of the Bureau of Public Roads
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau of Public Roads shall carry out the responsibility and authority of the Secretary with respect to Federal and Federal-aid highway construction, administration, research and development, and planning. More particularly, the Bureau shall: (1) In cooperation with the States, administer Federal laws pertaining to completion of a National System of Interstate and Defense Highways and construction of highways on the Federal-aid primary and secondary systems and their urban extensions, providing for scenic development and road beautification; (2) in cooperation with the U.S. Forest Service and State Highway departments, construct roads on the forest highway system; (3) construct selected main roads through public lands; (4) in cooperation with Central American Republics, survey and construct the Inter-American Highway; and (5) conduct other programs as authorized. The Bureau shall conduct planning and R&D programs and promote establishment of highway safety programs by the States, maintain liaison with groups concerned with highway safety, and maintain a national register containing information for State driver licensing authorities regarding drivers whose licenses have been revoked or suspended for certain safety-code violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau's responsibilities encompass construction, administration, R&D, interagency cooperation, international projects, promotion of state safety programs under uniform standards, liaison duties, and maintenance of a national driver register; these are operational priorities and program criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for issuance of facility license amendment (Atomic Energy Commission example)
rubrics_metrics.description: No request for a hearing or petition to intervene having been filed following publication of the notice of proposed action, the Atomic Energy Commission has issued Amendment No. 16 authorizing operation with the TRIGA Mark m core. The license was issued substantially as set forth in the notice of proposed issuance, with the exception of (1) minor editorial modifications in the license, (2) minor revisions in the Technical Specifications, and (3) a change described in an application amendment affecting drilled holes and permitted operation (air or water filled in-core region). The changes involve no significant hazards considerations greater than those previously evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no hearing/petition is filed, an agency may issue amendments substantially as proposed, allowing minor editorial and technical-spec changes and operational changes that do not increase hazards beyond previously evaluated limits. The notice documents the basis for finding 'no significant hazards' increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariff filing and complaint/investigation process (Civil Aeronautics Board example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A carrier's tariff revision proposing new rates (e.g., blocked-space parcel post rates) may be challenged by other carriers (complaint alleging contravention of prior Board decisions requiring space-available basis). A complaint can result in an order of investigation and suspension. Parties asserting adverse effects must advance supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tariff proposals must be consistent with applicable Board decisions (e.g., space-available requirement). Opponents may file complaints alleging adverse effects; the Board may investigate and suspend proposed rates pending resolution. Supporting data strengthens challenges.
